en: The *Kriyāsaṃgrahakārikā*:
the examination of the teacher and disciples, followed by the supplication to the teacher;
then the teacher should perform the service of the mantra, and thereafter the examination of the ground. (1)
Being joined in yoga with the deity and having performed the worship of the earth,
and having performed the ritual dismissal of the deity, one should then purify the ground.
Having sown barley seeds, one should also worship Jāṅgulī;
having carefully sprinkled the thread, one should examine the Vāstu-nāga.

Having correctly understood the characteristics of the bricks, one should then determine the directions; having correctly understood the income and expenditure, as well as the characteristics of the temple.
Having worshipped the gods, the guardians of the directions, and the earth according to the prescribed rite,
and having performed the planting of the *ītikā*, one should perform the *pramohana* fire-oblation.
Then, during the forest procession, the wise one should properly raise the door-frame;
having established the wooden beam at the top, he should offer oblations into the immortal fire.
In this [rite], there is the entry of the Vajrācārya, the cultivation of the three samādhis,
the circumambulation, the purpose of the sūtras, and the casting down of the colored powders.
Then, having completed the ritual procedure for the fire and the installation of the pedestal by means of the left-hand practice,
one should thereafter install the image.
Then, painting, the *vali*, the *piṇḍī*, and the characteristics of the *gaṇḍikā*;
as well as the consecration (*pratiṣṭhāna*) of these, and likewise the taking of the wandering life (*pravrajyā*). // 9 //

One should worship the maṇḍala of the Gaṇas by means of the characteristics of the dharmadhātus, the planting of victory banners, the restoration of what is decayed, and the gathering [of offerings]. (10)
The *Kriyāsaṃgrahakārikā* is completed.
This is the work of the venerable Nāgārjuna.
